- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.1) within 3–5 days, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to counteract mean reversion bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.0% to first 5–7 forecast points.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings (e.g., 0.00–0.05), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead by 0.5–1.0% to align with sentiment momentum.
